scenarios.title: Database connection pool exhaustion
scenarios.alert: the gateway is returning 504 Gateway Timeout errors on GET /orders
scenarios.ground_truth: order-service leaks database connections: the /orders/leaky code path acquires a pg pool client and never releases it. After 10 such requests the pool (max 10) is exhausted, every later GET /orders waits forever for a client, and the gateway's 3s upstream timeout turns that into 504s. Postgres itself is healthy.

precondition.description: GET /orders through the gateway times out with a 504.

scenarios.title: Memory leak with repeated OOM kills
scenarios.alert: the gateway is intermittently returning 502 Bad Gateway on /orders
scenarios.ground_truth: order-service leaks memory: its Idempotency-Key replay cache (src/idempotency.ts) keeps every request body and response in a module-level Map with no TTL or eviction. Under storefront's steady bulk-order traffic its memory grows until it reaches the 160 MiB container limit and the kernel OOM-kills it (exit 137); the on-failure restart policy restarts it, and the cycle repeats roughly every 90s. Requests during each restart fail with 502 at the gateway. Known evidence limit: Docker clears OOMKilled/ExitCode when the restart policy restarts the container, so the tools show the OOM only indirectly (restartCount climbing, uptime resetting, memory approaching memoryLimitMiB, repeated startup lines in the logs).

precondition.description: order-service runs with a memory limit, has been restarted at least twice by its restart policy, and storefront is running.

scenarios.title: Corrupt deploy breaking payload parsing
scenarios.alert: the gateway is returning 500 Internal Server Error on POST /orders
scenarios.ground_truth: A recent order-service deploy broke order payload parsing. The newest commit in its deploy history, "Refactor order payload parsing" (minutes before the errors began), changed src/payload.ts to read each line's price as a Money object (price.amount, price.currency.toUpperCase()), while clients still send price as a number. Every POST /orders now throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase') in normalizeMoney/normalizeLine and returns 500 immediately. GET /orders and the database are unaffected.

precondition.description: order-service is up (GET /health 200) and POST /orders through the gateway fails with an immediate 500.
